question.problem:
Given that 
${\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(t)\,\text{d}t=2\pi \,i+\pi \,j+(2-\pi )\,k,$ 
$c=i+u\,j,$
and 
${\int }_{0}^{\pi }c\cdot f(t)\,\text{d}t=0,$ what is the value of $u?$
question.worked_solution:
The dot product rule states that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\pi }c\cdot f(t)\,\text{d}t=c\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Applying the dot-product rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }c\cdot f(t)\,\text{d}t & =c\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(i+u\,j)\cdot (2\pi \,i+\pi \,j+(2-\pi )\,k) \\  & =2\pi +u\cdot \pi +0\cdot (2-\pi ) \\  & =\pi (2+u).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since ${\int }_{0}^{\pi }c\cdot f(t)\,\text{d}t=0,$ we must have $\pi (2+u)=0,$ which means that $u=-2.$
